6-Deoxyerythronolide B is the macrolide precursor to erythromycin antibiotics. It's synthesized by a type I polyketide synthase. In polyketide biosynthesis, the building blocks are typically acyl-CoA derivatives.

For 6-deoxyerythronolide B specifically, the biosynthesis starts with a propionyl-CoA starter unit, and then methylmalonyl-CoA extender units are added in successive condensation reactions. This is a well-studied biosynthetic pathway in which propionyl-CoA serves as the starter unit and methylmalonyl-CoA serves as the extender unit.
